correctness.rationale: Replayed RESULT.md lines 23–53 for F_q-linear multiplication-preserving maps, without a unitality condition. Each cycle is simple: multiplication by a basis vector isolates any nonzero coefficient in an ideal and iterated squares recover the basis. Projecting a homomorphism onto a target cycle, a nonzero restriction to one source cycle therefore injects and is surjective by equal dimension. Two surjective restrictions would force every product in the target to be zero because the source summands annihilate each other, a contradiction. For each active target the resulting isomorphism has one nonzero per matrix row by disjoint-product preservation and the independence of the target basis squares; the cyclic square equations force a shift and coefficients c,c²,…, with c^(2^ℓ−1)=1. Thus h=ℓg labels per source/target pair and (1+rh)^r maps. In a composition-idempotent map each selected source must select itself with the identity label, by cancellation in the group of isomorphisms; conversely these conditions suffice. With k identity loops all other targets independently have 1+kh choices, and projection onto the fixed cycles identifies the image with their direct sum, even when the image is embedded diagonally. This proves the histogram, image type and all ranks, including the zero map, singletons and characteristic two. Independently, all 65536 binary 4×4 matrices at ℓ=r=2 gave 25 homomorphisms and histogram (1,6,1) at ranks (0,2,4); ℓ=1,r=2 over F₂ gave 9 maps and (1,4,1). evidence: The indexed general proof requires identity labels on exactly the selected fixed cycles, then counts zero and each compatible fixed-source label independently. The older wreath-product theorem enumerates labelled full-transformation idempotents, yielding binom(d,k)(kh)^(d−k) on d participating points.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The indexed proof specializes to the same root rule and rank spectrum. Projecting a retract onto its fixed cycles makes its image algebra the claimed direct sum, so the image observation is not a distinct remainder. Also, once the partial wreath model is identified, restrict an idempotent to its defined domain of size d, use the older full-wreath count there, and sum over domain choices. For k>0 this gives Σ_d binom(r,d)binom(d,k)(kh)^(d−k)=binom(r,k)(1+kh)^(r−k); k=0 is the zero map. Thus the zero-inclusive combinatorics is a binomial transform of the known full-domain enumeration, not a new enumerative mechanism.
